terms.gloss: a set form, rule; a formula
evidence: Cic. Leg. 1.4 fin.: stipulātiōnum et jūdiciōrum fōrmulās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically a fixed form of words, above all in law, and a rule or pattern; Morgan–Owens gives it, after Gauss and nineteenth-century books of medicine, for a mathematical or chemical formula. Diminutive of fōrma.

phrases.latin: sunt jūra, sunt fōrmulae dē omnibus rēbus cōnstitūtae
phrases.english: there are laws, there are formulas laid down for every case

formula-o.html: The diminutive keeps the vowel of fōrma (see design). De Vaan 233–234, s.v. fōrma, prints the o long; Ernout–Meillet “stress the length of o”, which he takes for a recent lengthening of short o before r and a consonant (Leumann 1977: 114).

sources: Lewis & Short: formula · Lewis & Short: forma
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. formula (math.).
Michiel de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages (2008), pp. 233–234.
